html:
The Mande peoples are the West African peoples who speak Mande languages, among them the Soninke, the Malinke (Mandinka), the Bambara and the Dyula. The map's 900 snapshot stretches the name across a broad band of savanna and forest edge from the Atlantic coast to the lands near Lake Chad, wider than the Mande world really was.

The Soninke had already built Ghana (Wagadu), the first great empire of the western Sahel, which grew rich by sending gold north in the trans-Saharan trade. The much older stone villages of Dhar Tichitt may have been built by their ancestors.

Further south the Malinke lived in small chiefdoms on the upper Niger. In the 1200s they would found the Mali Empire under Sundiata Keita. Later, Dyula merchants carried Mande trade and Islam far to the south and east.
